MCI.verdict: The most dangerous attack in the league and it never takes its foot off: 2.44 xG per 90 when ahead, more than when level. Best chance quality going (0.14 a shot, 38 box touches).
MCI.fpl: Haaland is the armband every week they play a side that tries to play. The catch is Maresca: he rotates (2.2 changes a match) and hooks early (first change 56'), so anyone not called Haaland is a minutes gamble.
MCI.gw: Fulham want the ball and push up (58% possession, 1.34 xG conceded). That leaves space behind. Haaland captain.

FUL.verdict: A good-looking ball side that gets into the box (32 touches a match) and never panics: settled eleven, latest changes in the league (68').
FUL.fpl: Minutes are bankable, but they give chances away when level (1.43 per 90), so their defenders are not.
FUL.gw: Away at City: nothing from Fulham this week.

ARS.verdict: The best team in the league by a distance. They control games instead of chasing them: 0.74 xG conceded a match, 11 shots, and only 96 minutes behind all season.
ARS.fpl: The defence is the asset. Gabriel has started all 10 and played 90 every time. The goals spread across the attack, so no single forward is a lock.
ARS.gw: At Newcastle, who concede 1.98 xG per 90 when level but create little themselves (1.14 a match). Strong clean-sheet spot. A good week for Arsenal attackers too.

NEW.verdict: Chaos. They run hard, rotate, attack whatever the score and leave the door open (1.67 xG conceded). When the game is level they barely create (0.76 per 90).
NEW.fpl: Target attackers against them. Avoid their defenders.
NEW.gw: Arsenal at home: expect to be pinned back.

AVL.verdict: Good when level (1.73 made, 0.99 given), but they fall apart once ahead: 3.11 xG conceded per 90 when leading, and 16.6 shots conceded a match.
AVL.fpl: Villa defenders are a trap. Their games stay open, which suits N.Jackson and whoever faces them.
AVL.gw: Home to Sunderland, who shoot from good spots and chase hard when behind. If Villa score first, expect a reply. N.Jackson yes, Villa clean sheet no.

SUN.verdict: They shoot from good positions (0.13 a shot) but can't keep games tight (1.64 conceded) and have hardly led all season.
SUN.fpl: Nothing at the back. Attackers only in open games.
SUN.gw: At Villa: a game with goals at both ends.

BOU.verdict: The most complete side outside the top two. They win the ball back (27.7 a match), concede only 10.3 shots, create quality chances (0.13 a shot), and play the same whether ahead or level. Rose trusts his eleven and changes late.
BOU.fpl: Their defenders are real, which is why keeping Silva was right. Tavernier starts every week and gets good chances (4.2 xG).
BOU.gw: Home to Forest, who shoot from distance (0.09 a shot). A prime clean-sheet spot. Silva and Tavernier both good.

NFO.verdict: Deep block, win it back, break. Hard to break down (10 shots conceded a match), but they take long shots and only come alive once ahead.
NFO.fpl: Sneaky defenders, low-quality attack. Gibbs-White creates (2.6 xA) but has one goal.
NFO.gw: At Bournemouth: a hard week. Selling Gibbs-White now loses little.

CHE.verdict: Alonso's 3-4-2-1 rotates heavily (2.7 changes a match), leaks when level (1.8 per 90) and goes flat when behind (0.76).
CHE.fpl: Only the nailed core: Palmer and Rogers have started 10 of 10. Everyone else is a coin flip on minutes. The defence is not a buy.
CHE.gw: Home to Leeds, who are organised and run hard. Palmer and Rogers fine, not captain material this week.

LEE.verdict: Workmanlike and settled. They spend most of their football level (659 minutes) and rarely get into the box (19.8 touches).
LEE.fpl: Calvert-Lewin is the whole attack (4.4 xG). Bogle is nailed.
LEE.gw: At Chelsea, who leak when level: Calvert-Lewin has a shot.

COV.verdict: Lampard sits deep (39% possession), defends the box, protects a lead and goes flat behind. A low-event team.
COV.fpl: Rudoni is their threat (2.2 xG, 1.7 xA). Clean sheets are shaky (1.5 xG conceded).
COV.gw: Home to Palace, the worst defence in the league (2.17 xG conceded). Rudoni's best fixture of the run.

CRY.verdict: Under Sage, the softest side in the league: 2.17 xG and 18.9 shots conceded a match. Thomas Frank takes his first game: expect a tighter back three and more caution.
CRY.fpl: Attack them until Frank shows otherwise.
CRY.gw: At Coventry: a new-manager game, so a lift is possible, but the defence they inherit is the worst going.

TOT.verdict: De Zerbi's side has the ball (63%) but shoots from distance (0.08 a shot): sterile up front, solid at the back (1.2 conceded). Rotates and hooks early (56').
TOT.fpl: The value is at the back: Kinsky and Van Hecke. The attackers frustrate.
TOT.gw: Home to Ipswich, who concede 1.95 a match and open up further when chasing. Spurs' best attacking week, and a fair clean-sheet chance. Van Hecke good.

IPS.verdict: Open at both ends. They shoot well but concede 1.95 a match.
IPS.fpl: Davis is nailed, but the defence behind him is not a clean-sheet side, so selling him is right.

HUL.verdict: 5-4-1 low block with 33% of the ball, and they fold once ahead (2.29 conceded per 90 when leading).
HUL.gw: Brighton come with the second-best attack in the league.

BHA.verdict: Second-best attack (1.94 xG a match), a settled eleven, and they keep pushing when ahead (2.06). Loose when level (1.89 conceded).
BHA.fpl: Their attacking players: Groß (4 goals, 4 assists, 30 corners) and De Cuyper, a left winger FPL prices as a £5.5m defender (2 goals, 3 assists). Verbruggen is fine against weak attacks.
BHA.gw: At Hull's deep block: Brighton have the ball all day. Groß, De Cuyper and Verbruggen all good.

LIV.verdict: Iraola's Liverpool press and run, then sit once ahead (0.74 per 90 when leading) and only fire when behind (2.12).
LIV.fpl: Their attackers return in chase games. Their defenders do fine when protecting a lead (0.83 conceded per 90 when ahead).
LIV.gw: Home to an open United side: the game should stay open.

MUN.verdict: Open and chaotic: they win the ball back and chase hard but concede 1.75 a match. Carrick makes early changes.

EVE.verdict: Moyes's Everton are organised and settled, but they sit on leads and go flat behind. A low ceiling.
EVE.fpl: Barry carries the attack. Little else.

BRE.verdict: Comfortable without the ball: they win it back, defend the box and keep going once ahead (1.81 per 90). But they concede 15.5 shots a match.
BRE.fpl: Attackers in home games. The defence leaks shots.
BRE.gw: Home to Everton: tight, low scoring.

players.411: Captain. City attack whatever the score and Fulham leave space. 9 goals from 7.1 xG in 10 starts.
players.4: The best defender in the best defence, 90 minutes every game. At Newcastle: clean sheet plus a set-piece threat (1.4 xG).
players.566: Keep. Bournemouth are a real defence and Forest shoot from distance.
players.68: Nailed, quality chances (4.2 xG). Forest concede few shots, so a solid week, not a big one.
players.183: Coventry's main threat against the worst defence in the league. Best fixture of his run.
players.112: Spurs are solid at the back and Ipswich concede and chase. A fair clean-sheet shout.
players.124: Brighton dominate the ball at Hull. 4 goals, 4 assists; good.
players.115: Not a full-back: FPL lists him as a defender, but he has started all 10 at left wing. Crosses (89th percentile among left wingers), chances created (83rd) and 37% of Brighton's corners, with a defender's clean-sheet points. At Hull's deep block, good.
players.154: Nailed, 29 shots. Leeds are organised. Fine, not the armband.
players.40: Nailed, 5 goals. Same read as Palmer.
players.346: Leeds' whole attack. Chelsea leak when level. Playable.
players.166: Villa games stay open, and Sunderland reply. Good.
players.305: Ipswich are not a clean-sheet side. Selling is right.
players.31: Saliba is coming back. Selling is right.
players.480: Creates (2.6 xA) but one goal, and it is a hard week at Bournemouth. Selling loses little.
players.330: Nailed, but a hard week at Chelsea.
